title: Olleik Foods: the whole system, visitor, customer and admin
pronunciation: "Olleik" is written "Oh-lake" in the spoken text only; on screen it stays "Olleik"
rules: calm, short sentences; no marketing claims, no delivery-time promises, no spoken prices

lines.text: This film follows one restaurant through the whole Olleik system, from its first visit to its invoices.
lines.speak: This film follows one restaurant through the whole Oh-lake system, from its first visit to its invoices.
lines.caption: One restaurant, through the whole Olleik system

lines.text: On the left is what a visitor or customer sees on a phone. On the right is the Olleik admin, on a desktop.
lines.speak: On the left is what a visitor or customer sees on a phone. On the right is the Oh-lake admin, on a desktop.
lines.caption: Left: the customer's phone. Right: the admin

lines.text: When something on one side causes a change on the other, a line of light links the two. The categories on the public site come straight from the admin's category list.
lines.caption: Public categories come from the admin's list

lines.text: The public catalog page shows the same categories, each with its own page of products.
lines.caption: The public catalog shows the same categories

lines.text: Each category page lists the products the admin keeps active, with their photos. Prices stay private until a customer signs in.
lines.caption: Active products with photos, no public prices

lines.text: A restaurant owner wants to buy from Olleik. On the home page, they tap Become a customer.
lines.speak: A restaurant owner wants to buy from Oh-lake. On the home page, they tap Become a customer.
lines.caption: A restaurant owner taps Become a customer

lines.text: They fill in the application: business name, contact, email, phone and address.
lines.caption: The application form

lines.text: They add the type of business and a short note, and submit. Now watch the admin side. The application appears on the Leads page, marked new.
lines.caption: The application arrives in Leads, marked new

lines.text: The phone confirms that the application was received. The dashboard also lists it under Recent leads.
lines.caption: Also listed under Recent leads

lines.text: On the Leads page, tabs sort the applications by status: new, contacted, approved and rejected.
lines.caption: Leads are sorted by status

lines.text: The site also has a contact form and a supplier form. Those messages are saved, but the admin does not show them yet.
lines.caption: Contact and supplier forms: saved, not shown in the admin

lines.text: The site also has pages about the company, delivery and common questions.
lines.caption: About, delivery and questions pages

lines.text: On the Leads page, the admin reviews the application and marks it approved.
lines.caption: The admin marks the lead approved

lines.text: Approved leads wait on the Add a customer page. One click converts the lead into a customer account.
lines.caption: Convert the approved lead into a customer

lines.text: An account can also be created by hand, under Manual entry, for a customer who did not apply online.
lines.caption: Manual entry for customers who did not apply online

lines.text: The new account opens with a setup checklist. It is not invited yet, and it has no products.
lines.caption: A setup checklist for the new account

lines.text: The admin can send an invitation by email, or copy a one-time link to send by message. The customer opens it and sees a welcome page with their business name.
lines.caption: An invitation opens a welcome page

lines.text: They choose a password and save it. They are now signed in to their own portal, and on the admin side the account shows as active.
lines.caption: Signed in: the account is now active

lines.text: The welcome banner appears only on this first visit to the portal.
lines.caption: A welcome banner on the first visit

lines.text: Their catalog is still empty. Nothing is visible until the admin sets it up.
lines.caption: The catalog is empty until the admin sets it up

lines.text: The admin opens Add product and picks the items this restaurant buys.
lines.caption: The admin picks this customer's products

lines.text: As soon as they are added, the customer's catalog fills up. Each product shows a price marked Your price.
lines.caption: The catalog fills up, each price marked Your price

lines.text: Each price comes from the margin rules. The table shows the cost, the list price, the customer's price, the profit, and the rule behind it.
lines.caption: Cost, list price, customer price, profit and rule

lines.text: The admin can also type a price by hand. The customer sees the new price in their catalog.
lines.caption: A price typed by hand reaches the customer

lines.text: A margin for this customer reprices every product that follows the rules. Prices typed by hand stay as they are.
lines.caption: A customer margin reprices the computed prices

lines.text: Catalog visibility can open whole categories. The extra products show at the list price, without the Your price label.
lines.caption: Visibility opens whole categories at list price

lines.text: A hidden product disappears from this customer's catalog, even when it is assigned.
lines.caption: A hidden product disappears for this customer

lines.text: Assign products does the same for many customers at once, with a preview of cost and profit before anything changes.
lines.caption: Assign many products to many customers

lines.text: The Margin rules page holds the global, product, category and customer margins. A new rule updates the affected customer prices automatically.
lines.caption: A new margin rule updates prices automatically

lines.text: From the customer page, the admin can also recompute prices, change many prices at once, copy a catalog from another customer, or export it.
lines.caption: Recompute, bulk prices, copy a catalog, export

lines.text: Offers are set per customer. Here the admin creates a welcome offer on salmon, for two weeks.
lines.caption: The admin creates an offer for this customer

lines.text: The offer appears right away on the customer's Offers page.
lines.caption: It appears on the customer's Offers page

lines.text: In the catalog, the salmon now shows the offer price, with the regular price struck through.
lines.caption: The catalog shows the offer price

lines.text: An offer template can be applied to many customers in one step. The preview shows exactly what will change, and the customer sees the new offer.
lines.caption: A template applied to many customers at once

lines.text: Running now lists the active offers and each applied batch, which can be undone as a whole.
lines.caption: Running offers, and batches that can be undone

lines.text: Templates are reusable offers, such as a weekend promotion, kept in the Offer library.
lines.caption: Templates are reusable offers

lines.text: The customer searches the catalog and adds salmon to the cart.
lines.caption: The customer searches and adds to the cart

lines.text: They add cream, takeout cups and oat milk, choosing the quantities as they go.
lines.caption: Choosing quantities

lines.text: The cart shows the exact price of each line, including the offer.
lines.caption: The cart shows the exact prices

lines.text: At checkout they choose delivery or pickup, and can leave a note. There is no online payment. The order follows the account's payment terms.
lines.caption: Delivery or pickup, a note, no online payment

lines.text: They submit the order. Now watch the admin side. It appears at once in the New tab, with a number in the sidebar and an alert sound.
lines.caption: The order appears in New at once

lines.text: On the phone, the order shows as Received. The dashboard counts it as waiting for confirmation.
lines.caption: Received, and waiting for confirmation

lines.text: The admin opens the order. Each line shows its cost and profit, which the customer never sees.
lines.caption: Cost and profit, for the admin only

lines.text: The order also shows who placed it, with the note left at checkout.
lines.caption: The customer and the checkout note

lines.text: When the admin confirms, the system checks the stock. There are not enough takeout cups.
lines.caption: The stock check finds a shortage

lines.text: The admin confirms anyway. The stock is taken out, and on the customer's phone the order is now Confirmed.
lines.caption: Confirmed on both sides

lines.text: The cups are now unavailable to every customer. The oat milk came from an open category, so it is now part of this customer's catalog.
lines.caption: Cups unavailable, oat milk added to the catalog

lines.text: When the order is packed, the admin marks it prepared. The customer sees Ready.
lines.caption: Prepared for the admin, Ready for the customer

lines.text: Once it is handed over, the admin completes it, and the customer sees Completed.
lines.caption: Completed on both sides

lines.text: The customer's order page always shows the current status, and refreshes on its own.
lines.caption: The order page keeps itself up to date

lines.text: A second order can be cancelled, with a reason that stays with the admin. The customer sees Cancelled, and any stock taken for it goes back.
lines.caption: A cancelled order, on both sides

lines.text: Both sides keep the full order history, and the admin lists can be filtered by date.
lines.caption: Order history, filtered by date

lines.text: Each order has an invoice. Both sides print the same document, with the business details at the top.
lines.caption: The same invoice on both sides

lines.text: The customer's statement for a period matches the admin's customer copy.
lines.caption: The statement matches the customer copy

lines.text: A statement can be printed for any period, using the period filter at the top.
lines.caption: Statements for any period

lines.text: The admin also has an internal copy, with cost and profit, clearly marked as internal.
lines.caption: An internal copy with cost and profit

lines.text: A cancelled order keeps its invoice, marked as cancelled, for the record.
lines.caption: A cancelled invoice is kept for the record

lines.text: Back on the admin side, confirming the order reduced the stock. The cups now show as oversold.
lines.caption: The order reduced the stock

lines.text: The dashboard also lists today's top products and top customers, with links to the full analytics.
lines.caption: Top products and customers

lines.text: The dashboard shows today's revenue and profit, and flags the low stock.
lines.caption: Today's revenue, profit and low stock

lines.text: The dashboard also flags customers who were invited but have not signed in yet, so the team can follow up.
lines.caption: Invited customers who have not signed in

lines.text: The low-stock and unavailable statements list what needs reordering.
lines.caption: Low-stock and unavailable statements

lines.text: On the Products page, low and oversold stock is flagged in the stock column.
lines.caption: Stock flags on the Products page

lines.text: When new stock arrives, the admin receives it. It settles the oversold units first, and the cups are available again for customers.
lines.caption: Received stock makes the cups available again

lines.text: Analytics shows the revenue trend, best sellers, top customers, and customers who have gone quiet.
lines.caption: Analytics: trend, best sellers, customers

lines.text: Further down, analytics shows the best sellers by units, revenue and profit, and the products that are not moving.
lines.caption: Best sellers and slow movers

lines.text: The report builder prints a summary for any period. Adding cost and profit turns it into an internal report.
lines.caption: Reports for any period

lines.text: The product list can be printed for customers, or with cost columns for internal use.
lines.caption: The printable product list

lines.text: The admin adds a new product, with its photo, cost, price and starting stock.
lines.caption: A new product with its photo

lines.text: Once it is created, it appears on the public site, still without a price.
lines.caption: It appears on the public site

lines.text: When a product is set to inactive, it leaves the public site.
lines.caption: An inactive product leaves the public site

lines.text: It also leaves every customer's catalog.
lines.caption: And every customer's catalog

lines.text: Categories can have one level of subcategories, which customers see in their catalog filter.
lines.caption: Categories and subcategories

lines.text: When the admin edits the account, the customer's Account page shows the new details.
lines.caption: Account changes reach the customer

lines.text: If the account is suspended, the customer can no longer open the portal.
lines.caption: A suspended account is locked out

lines.text: Setting it back to active restores access, with the catalog and prices kept.
lines.caption: Active again, catalog and prices kept

lines.text: The customer list shows every account with its status, phone, payment terms and catalog size.
lines.caption: Every account in the customer list

lines.text: Customers can reset their own password from the sign-in page. Admins use a separate sign-in, open only to approved emails.
lines.caption: Password reset, and the admin sign-in

lines.text: Finally, order alerts can be switched on, so a sound plays when a new order arrives.
lines.caption: Order alerts with sound

lines.text: That is the full loop, from application to invoice, on both sides of Olleik.
lines.speak: That is the full loop, from application to invoice, on both sides of Oh-lake.
lines.caption: From application to invoice, on both sides
